questions.question: Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows. Statement: The city library reported that 90% of patrons who borrowed books last month utilized the online reservation system. Conclusions: I. The online reservation system is convenient for library patrons. II. 10% of patrons borrowed books without using the online reservation system.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows.

Statement: The city library reported that 90% of patrons who borrowed books last month utilized the online reservation system.

Conclusions:

I. The online reservation system is convenient for library patrons.

II. 10% of patrons borrowed books without using the online reservation system.
questions.solution:
Conclusion I: "The online reservation system is convenient for library patrons."

Not necessarily true. High usage does not automatically prove convenience; there may be other reasons for using it (e.g., requirement, limited availability).

Conclusion II: "10% of patrons borrowed books without using the online reservation system."

Follows directly from the statement: 100% − 90% = 10%

Here, Only Conclusion II follows.

questions.question: Instruction: Identify the assumptions that must hold for the statement to be valid, then choose the appropriate option. Statement: A sign reads: "Consumption of outside food and beverages is strictly prohibited within the cinema premises." Assumptions: I. The cinema sells food and beverages inside. II. Allowing outside food would reduce the cinema's concession revenue. III. Patrons will follow the prohibition rule.
questions.questionHtml:
Instruction: Identify the assumptions that must hold for the statement to be valid, then choose the appropriate option.

Statement: A sign reads: "Consumption of outside food and beverages is strictly prohibited within the cinema premises."

Assumptions: I. The cinema sells food and beverages inside.

II. Allowing outside food would reduce the cinema's concession revenue.

III. Patrons will follow the prohibition rule.

options.text: Only I and II are implicit
options.html: Only I and II are implicit

options.text: Only II and III are implicit
options.html: Only II and III are implicit

questions.solution:
Assumption I: Such prohibitions are generally imposed to promote in-house concessions, so this assumption is taken for granted. 

Assumption II:The restriction logically implies a financial or business reason, one of the most common being protection of concession sales. 

Assumption III: Any posted rule or sign assumes that people will comply, otherwise displaying it would serve no purpose. 

Here, All assumptions are implicit

questions.question: Identify the odd number: 2, 4, 8, 16, 30, 64
questions.questionHtml: Identify the odd number: 2, 4, 8, 16, 30, 64
questions.solution:
2 → 4
4 → 8
8 → 16
16 → 32 (but the number given is 30, which breaks the pattern)
Then 32 → 64

So, 30 does NOT follow the doubling pattern.
